Apple___Apple_scab.description: Fungal disease caused by Venturia inaequalis. Appears as dark, scabby spots on leaves and fruits, leading to reduced yield and quality.
Apple___Apple_scab.fertilizer: Apply a balanced NPK fertilizer (e.g., 10-10-10) to maintain overall plant vigor and follow with a copper-based fungicide as recommended.

Apple___Black_rot.description: Fungal disease caused by Botryosphaeria obtusa. Symptoms include dark leaf spots, fruit rot, and bark cankers.
Apple___Black_rot.fertilizer: Use a slow-release, well-balanced NPK fertilizer and avoid overwatering. Combine with appropriate fungicidal sprays for best management.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.description: Fungal disease caused by Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae. Characterized by yellow–orange lesions on leaves.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.fertilizer: Use a balanced orchard fertilizer and ensure proper soil drainage. Supplement with micronutrients like zinc and boron if soil tests indicate deficiency.

Apple___healthy.description: The apple leaf appears healthy with no visible disease symptoms or nutrient deficiencies.
Apple___healthy.fertilizer: Maintain regular fertilization using a balanced NPK (e.g., 14-14-14) and organic compost to support continuous growth and fruiting.

Blueberry___healthy.description: The blueberry leaf appears healthy and free from major disease or stress symptoms.
Blueberry___healthy.fertilizer: Apply an acid-forming fertilizer (e.g., ammonium sulfate) suitable for blueberries, keeping soil pH slightly acidic (4.5–5.5).

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.description: The cherry leaf appears healthy with uniform color and no visible lesions.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.fertilizer: Use a balanced fruit-tree fertilizer in early spring and add well-rotted manure or compost annually around the root zone.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.description: Fungal disease characterized by white, powdery growth on leaf surfaces, leading to distortion and reduced vigor.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.fertilizer: Apply a balanced fertilizer but avoid over-fertilizing with nitrogen. Combine with recommended fungicidal sprays and good air circulation.

Corn(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot.description: Caused by Cercospora zeae-maydis, producing gray to tan lesions with dark borders, often merging into large dead areas.
Corn(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot.fertilizer: Apply a nitrogen-rich but balanced fertilizer based on soil test results and rotate crops to reduce disease pressure.

Corn(maize)___Common_rust.description: Fungal disease caused by Puccinia sorghi, forming brown to reddish pustules on both sides of the leaf.
Corn(maize)___Common_rust.fertilizer: Maintain good soil fertility with a balanced NPK fertilizer and ensure adequate potassium to improve disease tolerance.

Corn(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.description: Caused by Exserohilum turcicum. Produces long, cigar-shaped gray-green lesions on leaves.
Corn(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.fertilizer: Use a complete NPK fertilizer along with organic matter to boost plant resilience. Avoid nutrient stress during early growth stages.

Corn(maize)___healthy.description: The corn leaf appears healthy with good color and no disease symptoms.
Corn(maize)___healthy.fertilizer: Apply a nitrogen-focused fertilizer (e.g., urea) in split doses along with adequate phosphorus and potassium as per soil test.

Grape___Black_rot.description: Fungal disease caused by Guignardia bidwellii. Causes dark lesions on leaves and shriveled, mummified fruits.
Grape___Black_rot.fertilizer: Use a vineyard fertilizer rich in potassium and magnesium, and avoid excessive nitrogen. Combine with regular fungicide sprays.

Grape___Esca(Black_Measles).description: Complex trunk disease causing dark streaks in wood and tiger-stripe patterns on leaves.
Grape___Esca(Black_Measles).fertilizer: Maintain balanced nutrition with NPK and micronutrients such as iron and magnesium. Avoid severe pruning stress and waterlogging.

Grape___Leaf_blight(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spot.description: Characterized by angular brown spots on leaves, often with yellow halos, leading to premature leaf drop.
Grape___Leaf_blight(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spot.fertilizer: Apply a balanced fertilizer including micronutrients like zinc and manganese, and ensure proper canopy management.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial disease caused by Xanthomonas campestris. Produces water-soaked lesions on leaves and fruit.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.fertilizer: Use a balanced orchard fertilizer and avoid excessive nitrogen that can increase susceptibility. Ensure good potassium levels.

Peach___healthy.description: Peach leaf appears healthy with no visible disease lesions or discoloration.
Peach___healthy.fertilizer: Apply a complete fruit-tree fertilizer in early spring and incorporate compost to maintain soil structure.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial disease caused by Xanthomonas species, producing small, water-soaked brown lesions on leaves and fruits.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.fertilizer: Use a balanced vegetable fertilizer and avoid overhead irrigation. Ensure adequate calcium and potassium.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.description: The bell pepper leaf appears healthy with uniform green color.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.fertilizer: Apply a vegetable-specific NPK fertilizer (e.g., 12-15-20) with calcium supplementation to prevent blossom end rot.

Potato___Early_blight.description: Fungal disease caused by Alternaria solani. Shows concentric ring (target-like) spots on older leaves.
Potato___Early_blight.fertilizer: Apply a balanced fertilizer with higher potassium content to improve tuber quality and use recommended fungicides.

Potato___Late_blight.description: Serious disease caused by Phytophthora infestans. Produces water-soaked lesions, white mold on undersides, and tuber rot.
Potato___Late_blight.fertilizer: Follow soil test–based fertilization with adequate phosphorus and potassium, and avoid excessive canopy density from high nitrogen.

Potato___healthy.description: Healthy potato leaf with no visible lesions or chlorosis.
Potato___healthy.fertilizer: Apply a potato-specific fertilizer rich in potassium and maintain slightly acidic soil.

Raspberry___healthy.description: Raspberry leaf appears healthy with good color and no disease symptoms.
Raspberry___healthy.fertilizer: Use a berry fertilizer high in potassium and organic mulches to conserve moisture and improve soil health.

Soybean___healthy.description: Soybean foliage is healthy and uniform with no visible disease.
Soybean___healthy.fertilizer: Ensure sufficient phosphorus and potassium, and inoculate seeds with Rhizobium for good nitrogen fixation.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.description: Fungal disease characterized by white powdery growth on leaf surfaces, causing yellowing and premature leaf drop.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.fertilizer: Use a balanced fertilizer while avoiding excessive nitrogen. Improve air circulation and apply recommended fungicides.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.description: Fungal disease causing small, purple to brown spots that merge, giving leaves a scorched appearance.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.fertilizer: Apply a berry fertilizer with balanced NPK and add organic mulch. Avoid overhead watering to reduce leaf wetness.

Strawberry___healthy.description: Healthy strawberry foliage with no spotting or chlorosis.
Strawberry___healthy.fertilizer: Use a strawberry-specific fertilizer applied in early spring and after harvest, combined with compost.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial disease causing greasy, small dark lesions on leaves, stems, and fruits.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.fertilizer: Use a balanced fertilizer with adequate calcium and avoid excessive nitrogen. Copper-based sprays may be used as recommended.

Tomato___Early_blight.description: Fungal disease caused by Alternaria solani, producing concentric ring lesions on older leaves.
Tomato___Early_blight.fertilizer: Apply a tomato fertilizer rich in potassium and maintain consistent watering. Combine with fungicide schedule.

Tomato___Late_blight.description: Aggressive disease caused by Phytophthora infestans. Causes large, irregular water-soaked lesions on leaves and fruits.
Tomato___Late_blight.fertilizer: Follow balanced NPK application and avoid dense planting. Use resistant varieties and protect with fungicides where necessary.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.description: Fungal disease caused by Passalora fulva. Yellowing on upper leaves with olive-green mold on the undersides.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.fertilizer: Maintain moderate nitrogen levels and improve air circulation. Use appropriate fungicides under humid conditions.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.description: Fungal disease causing numerous small, circular spots with dark margins on lower leaves.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.fertilizer: Apply balanced fertilizer and remove infected debris. Ensure sufficient potassium to improve disease resistance.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.description: Pest infestation by spider mites causing stippling, bronzing, and webbing on leaves.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.fertilizer: Maintain plant vigor with balanced fertilization and avoid water stress. Integrate biological or chemical mite control as needed.

Tomato___Target_Spot.description: Fungal disease causing dark concentric lesions on leaves, stems, and fruit.
Tomato___Target_Spot.fertilizer: Provide balanced nutrients with an emphasis on potassium and calcium and avoid overcrowding of plants.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: Viral disease transmitted by whiteflies, leading to leaf curling, yellowing, and stunted growth.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.fertilizer: Use a complete fertilizer with micronutrients to support recovery and focus on vector (whitefly) control.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: Viral disease causing mosaic or mottled patterns on leaves and reduced yield.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.fertilizer: Maintain good nutrition with NPK and micronutrients, remove infected plants, and practice strict hygiene.

Tomato___healthy.description: The tomato leaf appears healthy with no visible disease symptoms.
Tomato___healthy.fertilizer: Use a tomato-specific fertilizer rich in phosphorus and potassium, and add organic compost for long-term soil health.
